title: What happens if you shelter under a manchineel tree in the rain?

lines.text: Would you shelter under this tree in a storm? It's the most dangerous tree on Earth.
The manchineel is full of a milky sap that burns skin.
Rain washes the sap off the leaves and onto you. Your skin blisters.
Then you eat one of its sweet little apples. A doctor really did.
Her mouth burned like pepper. Her throat swelled until she could barely swallow.
Its Spanish name means little apple of death. Some trunks get a red warning band.
She recovered. You survived. Comment what you want to know next.

experiment.note: First beach set + manchineel tree, rain fx, apple prop. Hypothesis: a dare hook on a vivid 'deadliest tree' premise holds the first 3 s.

facts.claim: Manchineel (Hippomane mancinella) sap blisters skin; standing under it in rain can blister you because rain carries the sap
Guinness lists it as the world's most dangerous tree
Radiologist Nicola Strickland ate a manchineel 'beach apple' on holiday in Tobago: sweet at first, then peppery burning and a throat so tight she could hardly swallow; she recovered
Spanish name manzanilla de la muerte ('little apple of death'); trees are often marked with a red band or X
